graph.name: MailUp Group Messaging API Architecture
graph.notes: MailUp Group's Messaging API platform allows clients to schedule and send marketing campaigns via instant messaging applications. Frontend assets are hosted on S3 via CloudFront, API calls are handled by ECS microservices via ALB, asynchronous events are processed via SQS, with ElastiCache Redis, Multi-AZ RDS MySQL, and DynamoDB backing data requirements.

nodes.name: CloudFront
nodes.notes: Delivers the Single Page Application frontend and static marketing resources.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores SPA assets and marketing campaign content.

nodes.name: ALB
nodes.notes: Application Load Balancer distributing incoming API requests to ECS container microservices.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Cluster hosting API microservices (auth, bot, URL shortening, webhooks) and worker tasks.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Decouples microservices and buffers real-time or scheduled event messages for worker processing.

nodes.name: ElastiCache
nodes.notes: Redis application-level caching layer to reduce database load.

nodes.name: RDS MySQL
nodes.notes: Multi-AZ MySQL relational database for persistent application data.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Key-value store recording real-time events generated on the platform.

edges.notes: CloudFront fetches web assets and single page application files from S3.
Single Page Application makes API calls routed to the Application Load Balancer.
ALB routes incoming REST API traffic to microservices running on the ECS cluster.
ECS microservices publish scheduled or real-time event messages to SQS.
ECS worker tasks pull messages from SQS to process campaign sending and events.
ECS microservices query ElastiCache Redis for fast data caching.
ECS microservices persist structured relational data in Multi-AZ RDS MySQL.
ECS microservices record high-throughput event logs directly in DynamoDB.
